title: ACME Edge Pilot — scoping call (SOC2, SSO, RBAC, benchmarks)
summary: POC scoping focused on security gating (SOC 2/ISO evidence, SSO/SAML integration, RBAC and audit logs) plus workload sizing and benchmark plan. Agreed success criteria: SOC2 scope verified, SSO integration in staging, p99 latency <150ms for 512-token prompts on dedicated pool, throughput 120 qps with batching. Next: SE to run baseline benchmarks with customer prompt set, Redwood to provide SOC2 attestation and sample audit log schema, schedule trial Dedicated cluster for 2-week run.
topics: Security/compliance: SOC 2 Type II scope, ISO 27001 questions
Authentication: SSO/SAML, Okta integration, SCIM user provisioning
Authorization: RBAC model and admin roles
Observability: audit logs, token-level cost, retention
Workload sizing: tokens per request, concurrency, expected QPS
Benchmarks: p50/p95/p99 latency, throughput, model variants
Timeline and success criteria for pilot

transcript:
Meeting header
Date/Time: 2025-04-11 15:00 UTC
Duration: 55 mins
Attendees: Jordan Park (Redwood AE), Maya Chen (Redwood SE), Liam O'Neill (CSM); Ravi Patel (VP Eng), Sofia Martinez (Head of Security), Ben Carter (ML Infra), Tina Huang (PM)

[00:00] Jordan Park: all right hi everyone, thanks for taking the time. I'm Jordan, I'm the AE on this account. quick round-robin real quick?
[00:10] Ravi Patel: hi, Ravi here. VP engineering at Acme Edge. we're running a multimodal inference stack, looking to pilot Redwood for customer-facing summarization and chat features.
[00:20] Sofia Martinez: Sofia, head of security. I'm focused on the compliance gating — SOC 2, ISO evidence, data residency.
[00:26] Ben Carter: Ben — lead of ML infra, i'll handle the benchmarking and infra side.
[00:31] Tina Huang: Tina product. i'll coordinate acceptance criteria and product side.
[00:35] Jordan Park: great. Maya from our side will lead the technical bench and run experiments. Maya?
[00:40] Maya Chen: yep hi. we'll want your sample prompt set and typical payload sizes. initial ask is just to get a realistic workload so we can size Dedicated pool.
[00:48] [00:50] Jordan Park: the agenda today: security posture check, pilot success criteria, workload sizing, benchmark plan, timeline.
[00:56] Ravi Patel: on security, the primary blockers for us are SOC 2 scope and SSO. we need to know if Redwood can be onboarded under our Okta tenancy (SAML) and whether audit logs include user email + request body hashes.
[01:12] Sofia Martinez: yes and also retention windows — we need logs for 1 year for e-discovery requests. can Redwood provide log retention configuration or export hooks?
[01:22] Maya Chen: short answer: yes for export hooks; we can stream audit logs to your S3 or to your SIEM. retention policies are configurable in Private and Dedicated modes; hosted has retention tiers. i'll follow up with the schema for the audit events.
[01:35] Ben Carter: is there an example schema? curious how verbose the logs are and whether they contain prompt text or only hashes.
[01:42] Maya Chen: typically we redact or hash prompt text in logs for hosted; in Dedicated/Private you can opt into full logs but you need to accept data residency. i'll send an example — note sometimes the transcriber writes KV cache as 'KV cash' so apologies if we smoke that up in notes.
[01:58] Jordan Park: on SOC 2, we'll share our latest Type II report and a controls-in-scope spreadsheet. Sofia, does that work as a starting point?
[02:06] Sofia Martinez: yes, but we need to confirm which controls cover model hosting, key management, and network isolation — specifically KMS/HSM integration and VPC peering or private link.
[02:18] Jordan Park: Redwood supports KMS integrations (customer-managed keys) and has private VPC peering options in Private deployment; Dedicated can be placed in a customer VPC with strict egress rules. I'll include our KMS whitepaper.
[02:32] Tina Huang: timeline question — we want a 2-week pilot to validate latency/throughput and workflows. how quickly can Redwood stand up a Dedicated pool?
[02:42] Maya Chen: with tenant-prep and creds we can provision a small dedicated cluster in ~5 business days; full networking and SSO config can add time. for the pilot we're thinking a small 4-GPU pool to start.
[02:54] Ravi Patel: ok concrete success criteria from product/security perspective?
[03:00] Tina Huang: product wants latency p99 <150ms for 512-token prompts and acceptable quality compared to current baseline. also need functional SSO and RBAC for admins.
[03:09] Sofia Martinez: security wants SOC 2 evidence for the pilot scope, SAML sign-on working into staging, audit logs accessible, KMS for key control, and a contract addendum for data handling.
[03:22] Ben Carter: infra wants throughput of roughly 120 qps with batching enabled -- that's our expected peak -- and ability to sustain 20 concurrent long-context sessions with KV cache warm.
[03:35] Maya Chen: good, that gives us measurable targets. we'll propose a benchmark matrix: p50/p95/p99 latency for 128/512/2048 token contexts, throughput tests with continuous 10m and 1h windows, cold vs warm KV cache, and model quality evaluation using your labeled prompt set.
[03:54] Jordan Park: on model variants: do you want to test quantized variants? we can run q4 and int8 profiles. quantization affects latency and quality so we should include both.
[04:05] Ben Carter: yes include q4 and the float variant if possible. cost tradeoffs matter.
[04:10] Maya Chen: noted. we'll run redwood-llama-13b-q4 and redwood-guanaco-7b as examples — if you have a different preferred model, send it.
[04:20] Ravi Patel: about SSO — we use Okta, SCIM for provisioning. do you support Just-In-Time provisioning or do you need us to create service accounts?
[04:29] Jordan Park: we support SAML SSO and SCIM provisioning; JIT may depend on your IdP settings. common pattern is to provision test users first. we'll document the steps.
[04:39] Sofia Martinez: auditability question — will audit logs show tokenization or full prompt content? we can't keep full PII in plain logs.
[04:47] Maya Chen: default hosted pipeline hashes prompts, Dedicated gives you the option to keep full data inside your VPC. for compliance we recommend Dedicated or Private for PII workloads.
[04:58] Ben Carter: ok. for benchmarking, do you have a standard harness? we want reproducible runs so we can compare results across vendors.
[05:05] Maya Chen: yes, we have a bench harness (benchmarks-config.yml) that runs load with continuous arrival process; it measures latency percentiles, GPU utilization, and per-token cost. we'll share config and a script to replay your prompt set.
[05:18] Tina Huang: regarding pass/fail what decides pilot success?
[05:22] Jordan Park: let's codify: 1) SOC 2 attestation confirmed for pilot scope, 2) SSO + RBAC tested in staging, 3) p99 latency <150ms at target QPS for representative 512-token workload, 4) audit logs accessible and exportable, 5) product sign-off on quality metrics. if all met, move to a 90-day expansion.
[05:44] Sofia Martinez: timeline wise, we need everything to wrap before end of May to align with our vendor onboarding window.
[05:53] Jordan Park: that gives us about 6 weeks. feasible.
[05:57] [06:00] --- mid-call technical dive ---
[06:05] Maya Chen: Olivia (not here) sorry wrong name — um focusing on the bench: for the 120 qps target, do you expect requests to be uniformly 512 tokens or a mixture?
[06:14] Ben Carter: mixture — 60% under 512, 30% 512-1024, 10% long 2k sequences. average 480 tokens per request.
[06:23] Maya Chen: that distribution will influence kernel selection and the batching strategy. our runtime will pick kernels dynamically and keep KV cache across sessions to reduce load for long-contexts. we should run cold vs warm cache tests.
[06:37] Ravi Patel: any rough cost estimate for a 2-week pilot on a 4-GPU pool? ballpark so we can budget.
[06:44] Jordan Park: we'll provide pricing options: short pilot pricing and committed monthly for Dedicated. for the pilot ballpark maybe $6-8k depending on model and throughput. we'll send formal pricing.
[06:56] Tina Huang: can we run a tiny canary on hosted first before Dedicated, to validate auth and flows?
[07:01] Maya Chen: yes hosted API is fastest to validate SSO and functional flows; only thing is retention and data isolation differ. we often do hosted smoke + Dedicated benchmark.
[07:10] Sofia Martinez: on KMS if we provide customer-managed keys, do you support HSM-backed keys?
[07:16] Maya Chen: yes we integrate with common cloud KMS and can support HSM-backed keys depending on provider; we'll include the KMS integration guide.
[07:25] Ben Carter: about audit logs schema again, can you give a sample line?
[07:29] Maya Chen: example: timestamp, request_id, user_email, model_name, token_count, latency_ms, prompt_hash, response_hash, status. we'll send a CSV example.
[07:43] Jordan Park: ok recap real quick: we'll share SOC 2 and ISO posture, Maya will run initial bench, Ben will upload prompts, Sofia will provide SAML metadata.
[07:54] Ravi Patel: one more compliance ask: do you provide dedicated network egress controls for outbound model downloads? we can't have external network calls during pilot run.
[08:03] Maya Chen: Dedicated/Private supports egress lock-down; we can disable internet egress from the cluster and only allow internal artifact registries. note that some model downloads happen at provisioning time so we can pre-load models in air-gapped customers.
[08:20] Tina Huang: acceptance testing — product will have a 20-sample QA set to score quality. can Redwood ingest our labels and produce evaluation metrics?
[08:28] Maya Chen: yes we have eval tooling; we'll run quality regression checks and share a metrics dashboard.
[08:33] Ben Carter: good. any red flags around legal or procurement?
[08:36] Jordan Park: procurement will want the data handling addendum — we can prep a draft to attach to the contract.
[08:42] Sofia Martinez: please include SLA for uptime during pilot window.
[08:46] Jordan Park: noted. we'll propose a pilot SLA.
[08:49] [09:00] --- closing and logistics ---
[09:02] Jordan Park: next steps recap: Maya runs bench and shares results; Ben uploads prompt set; Jordan sends SOC docs; Sofia provides SAML metadata; Liam will draft runbook. we'll aim to meet the dates we listed.
[09:15] Ravi Patel: sounds good. any blockers from Redwood side?
[09:18] Maya Chen: none immediate. just need prompts and credentials.
[09:21] Tina Huang: i'll coordinate calendars for pilot start.
[09:24] Jordan Park: great. thanks everyone — we'll follow up via email and share the artifacts.
[09:29] Sofia Martinez: thanks.
[09:30] Ben Carter: cheers.
[54:10] [END]
